\begin{abstract}
We present \textbf{ADCD} (Asymptotic Dictionary Correction Discovery), a
deterministic framework for recovering structured corrections to known physical
laws from noisy data.
Given a classical baseline, ADCD searches for the residual correction that
vanishes exactly at the classical limit, using three interlocking mechanisms:
algebraically regularized primitives that enforce asymptotic vanishing as an
exact algebraic identity; a five-dimensional (MLT$\Theta$Q) Buckingham-$\pi$
engine that auto-derives dimensionless ratio arguments without manual
specification; and a Phenomenon-Specific Taxonomy encoding peer-reviewed
functional priors for each physics domain.
A four-step validation protocol---budget disclosure, positive control, BIC-based
ablation control, and determinism check---issues one of two verdicts:
IDENTIFIABLE or WITHHELD.
On three canonical scenarios at historical low-signal windows, Screened Coulomb
($\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=30.65$, exact symbolic match) and Entropy Expansion
($\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=14.70$, class-level match) are IDENTIFIABLE;
Time Dilation at $v\le0.3c$ is WITHHELD because the $4.8\%$ correction is
indistinguishable from 1\% noise---the intended, epistemically honest behavior.
All results are byte-exact deterministic.

\vspace{0.3em}
\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} symbolic regression; correction discovery;
dimensional analysis; Bayesian prior; model selection; identifiability
\end{abstract}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Introduction}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

In the expanding landscape of machine learning for the physical sciences~\cite{carleo2019,wang2023},
physical laws frequently take a correction-first form: a known classical baseline
extended by a term that vanishes at the classical
limit~\cite{einstein1905,debye1923,callen1985}.
Recovering that correction from observational data is distinct from full equation
discovery: the baseline is fixed, only the residual must be identified, and that
residual must vanish exactly where classical physics holds.

General-purpose symbolic regression (SR) engines such as
PySR~\cite{cranmer2020,cranmer2023}, AI Feynman~\cite{udrescu2020}, and
PhySO~\cite{tenachi2023} excel at equation discovery from scratch but face
three difficulties in the correction-first setting:
(i)~\emph{catastrophic cancellation}: floating-point precision collapses as
$u\to0$, corrupting optimizer feedback~\cite{ieee754};
(ii)~\emph{stochastic irreproducibility}: evolutionary search cannot guarantee
byte-identical results across runs~\cite{bongard2007,schmidt2009}; and
(iii)~\emph{silent overclaiming}: a single best-fit equation is returned
regardless of whether the data carry sufficient power to distinguish competing
structures~\cite{lacava2021}, generating what recent meta-science critiques identify
as an illusion of understanding~\cite{messeri2024,krenn2022}.
ADCD addresses each failure mode in turn: algebraically regularized primitives
eliminate cancellation; deterministic grammar enumeration ensures reproducibility;
explicit BIC-based identifiability gating prevents overclaiming.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Related Work}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

Automated scientific discovery traces back to pioneering heuristic systems such as
BACON~\cite{langley1987} and has evolved toward modern autonomous equation
discovery~\cite{kramer2026,makke2024,karagiorgi2022}.
General SR engines (Eureqa~\cite{schmidt2009}, PySR~\cite{cranmer2020,cranmer2023},
AI Feynman~\cite{udrescu2020,udrescu2020b}, PhySO~\cite{tenachi2023})
target unconstrained equation recovery and do not enforce classical-limit
constraints algebraically.
SINDy~\cite{brunton2016} shares our library-based approach but discovers
governing equations rather than corrections.
PINNs~\cite{raissi2019,karniadakis2021} embed physical laws as soft loss penalties;
ADCD imposes them as hard algebraic identities before any numerical computation.
Recent systems combining data with background knowledge and axiomatic reasoning,
such as AI-Descartes~\cite{cornelio2023} and AI~Hilbert~\cite{corywright2024},
highlight the importance of theory-grounded discovery, but do not address
catastrophic cancellation near asymptotic limits or provide formal identifiability gating.
While dimensional analysis and symmetry constraints have been integrated into
SR and dynamical learning~\cite{tenachi2023,petersen2021,otto2025},
ADCD extends this with a full five-dimensional (MLT$\Theta$Q) Buckingham-$\pi$ engine,
transcendental argument safety, and BIC-based identifiability reporting
in a single pre-fitting gate cascade.
To our knowledge, ADCD is the first framework to combine deterministic grammar
enumeration, algebraic classical-limit enforcement, phenomenon-specific Bayesian
priors, and explicit identifiability gating for the correction-first paradigm.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Methods}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

\subsection{Problem formulation}

Let $y_\mathrm{obs}$ and $y_\mathrm{cl}$ be the observed target and classical
prediction. The correction residual is:
\begin{equation}
  \Delta =
  \begin{cases}
    y_\mathrm{obs}/y_\mathrm{cl} - 1 & \text{(multiplicative)} \\
    y_\mathrm{obs} - y_\mathrm{cl}   & \text{(additive)}
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}
The mode with the lower scale dependence is selected, measured as the absolute
Spearman correlation between $|y_\mathrm{cl}|$ and the residual magnitude (ties
go to additive). There is no numeric ambiguity threshold: additive is used by
construction when $\mathrm{std}(y_\mathrm{cl})<10^{-15}$, when fewer than 5
valid points remain, or when both correlations vanish.
ADCD searches for $\hat{\Delta}(\mathbf{x};\boldsymbol{\theta})$ such that
$\hat{\Delta}\to0$ as the relevant dimensionless ratio $u\to0$.

\subsection{Algebraically regularized primitive dictionary}

Each primitive $D(u)$ satisfies $\lim_{u\to 0} D(u) = 0$ as an exact algebraic
identity, eliminating catastrophic cancellation.
For example, the naive form $(1-u)^{-1/2}-1$ collapses to $0.0$ at
$u=10^{-16}$ in \texttt{float64}; the regularized form
$u/[\sqrt{1-u}(\sqrt{1-u}+1)]$ returns $5.0\times10^{-17}$ at the same input.
Table~\ref{tab:primitives} lists all eight primitives.

Column ``Physical origin'' cites the fundamental equation that produces this
functional family; it does not imply the primitive is restricted to that domain.}

\texttt{D\_rat}      & $u/(1-u)$                       & $u\neq 1$   & Yukawa/Fermi pole \\
\texttt{D\_exp}      & $e^{-u}-1$                      & all $u$     & Debye/Yukawa screening \\
\texttt{D\_log}      & $\ln(1+u)$                      & $u>-1$      & Entropy of mixing \\
\texttt{D\_sqrt\_inv}& $1/\sqrt{1+u}-1$                & $u>-1$      & Gravitational / Coulomb potential \\
\texttt{D\_pow}      & $|u|^{|\theta|}$                & $u\ge0$     & Power-law corrections \\
\texttt{D\_osc}      & $1-\cos u$                      & all $u$     & Wave / AC oscillatory \\
\texttt{D\_sat}      & $\tanh u$                       & all $u$     & Magnetic / sigmoid saturation \\

\subsection{Dimensional grouping and free-scale generation}
\label{sec:buckingham}

ADCD employs a 5D (MLT$\Theta$Q) dimensional engine representing each
variable as $\mathbf{d}\in\mathbb{Z}^5$ over the SI base dimensions M, L, T,
$\Theta$, and Q.
Rather than computing the full rational nullspace, dimensionless arguments are generated via a two-pass domain heuristic: 
first, it groups physical variables with identical dimensions into pairwise ratios (e.g., $q_1/q_2$); 
second, each dimensional variable is normalized by linear and quadratic free-scale parameters ($v/\theta_{2k}, v^2/\theta_{2k+1}$; e.g., $r/\theta_4$).
Extending from the conventional 3D MLT to 5D is essential for correctness:
in a 3D engine charges $q_1,q_2$ are dimensionless scalars and incorrectly bypass the ratio generation;
in the 5D engine, charge carries genuine Charge dimension (Q), ensuring $q_1,q_2$ form pairwise ratios in Pass~1 and consume four free-scale parameters ($\theta_0\text{--}\theta_3$) in Pass~2 before distances are indexed.
Because four charge-dimensional candidates are enumerated first, that ratio
receives subscript $\theta_4$, not $\theta_0$.
This subscript is machine-verifiable evidence of automated discovery:
a manually supplied ratio would be pinned to $\theta_0$ by convention,
not assigned by enumeration.

\subsection{Phenomenon-specific taxonomy as Bayesian prior}
\label{sec:taxonomy}

Each physics phenomenon maps to a named set of permitted primitive families
derived exclusively from its fundamental equations.
For example, \texttt{yukawa\_debye\_screening} permits only \texttt{D\_exp}
and \texttt{D\_rat}: the Klein-Gordon equation yields $V\propto e^{-mr}/r$ and
Debye-H\"{u}ckel theory yields $\phi\propto e^{-r/\lambda_D}/r$; both involve
only exponential and rational families.
The taxonomy restricts \emph{which family} is searched; it says nothing about
\emph{which variable} enters the argument or \emph{what the scale is}---both
are determined by the Buckingham-$\pi$ engine and numerical optimizer.
Including a physically unjustified primitive acts as a noise sponge, collapsing
the Ablation Control BIC gap and destroying identifiability.
Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy} lists entries for our three experiments.

A $3\times3$ cross-misspecification audit (Appendix~\ref{app:misspec}, Table~\ref{tab:app_misspec}) confirms the taxonomy is \emph{safe against misspecification}: in all~6
wrong-taxonomy trials the system returned WITHHELD (0\% false discovery rate;
4 of the 6 are informative, since the 2 Time Dilation trials are WITHHELD even
under the correct prior; e.g., applying the oscillatory \texttt{wave\_resonance} prior to Screened Coulomb yields WITHHELD with $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=-910.5$).\footnote{Full supplementary audit tables are provided in Appendix~\ref{app:audits} and at \url{https://github.com/apiprdt/PhysicsPaper/tree/PythonADCD/rebuttal}.}
An incorrect prior causes conservative abstention, not hallucinated laws.

\subsection{Grammar enumeration and theta-intact constraint}

Candidates take the form $\hat{\Delta}=\theta_0\cdot D_i(u_{ij})$, optionally
extended with a secondary additive or multiplicative-coupled term ($\theta_0 D_a(u)+\theta_1 D_b(u)$ or $\theta_0 D_a(u)[1+\theta_1 D_b(u)]$; depth $\le3$, $\le25$ tokens).
Dimensionless arguments are auto-generated by the Buckingham-$\pi$ engine
(up to 12 candidate ratios per scenario).
All gates (Table~\ref{tab:gates}) are evaluated on the \emph{theta-intact}
expression---the fully parameterized symbolic form before any $\theta_i$ is
assigned the value $1$---because early substitution collapses dimensionful scale
parameters (e.g., $r/\theta_4$ representing a Debye length) to dimensionless
constants, falsifying the dimensional consistency check.

\subsection{Physical gate cascade}
\label{sec:gates}

Before fitting, each candidate must pass a five-gate cascade
(Table~\ref{tab:gates}) applied to the theta-intact expression.

\begin{table}[ht]
\small
\caption{The five-gate pre-fitting physical cascade.}
\label{tab:gates}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{3.5cm}p{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
Gate & Rejection criterion \\
\midrule
1. AST complexity & SymPy tree depth $>12$ or token count $>50$. \\
2. Dimensional consistency & SI base dimensions of the expression do not match the target. \\
3. Transcendental safety & Arguments to $\exp$, $\ln$, $\sqrt{\cdot}$ are not dimensionless. \\
4. Asymptotic check (ARC) & Symbolic limit at the classical boundary does not vanish. \\
5. Coarse numerical fitness & Evaluation at $\boldsymbol{\theta}=\mathbf{1}$ produces \texttt{NaN}/\texttt{Inf}. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Parameter optimization and model selection}

The top-ranked Stage-1 surviving candidates ($K=30$) are optimized via L-BFGS-B (JAX, \texttt{float64}).
Parameters are log-reparameterized ($\theta_i{=}s_i e^{u_i}$,
$s_i{\in}\{-1,+1\}$) for order-of-magnitude traversal; multiple restarts
reduce sensitivity to local optima.
Model selection uses an Extended BIC~\cite{schwarz1978,chen2008}: $\mathrm{BIC}=k\ln N - 2\ln\hat{L} + 2\ln|\mathcal{C}|$,
incorporating a multiple-testing penalty over the search space size $|\mathcal{C}|$.
By the Kass--Raftery scale~\cite{kass1995}, $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}>10$ is the
adopted identifiability threshold.

\subsection{Four-step validation protocol}
\label{sec:protocol}

The pipeline issues an IDENTIFIABLE verdict only when all four checks pass:
\begin{enumerate}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]
  \item \textbf{Budget disclosure.} The complete size of the domain-guided
        search space $|\mathcal{C}|$ and the primitive list are reported before any results are seen.
  \item \textbf{Positive control.} Restricted to the ground-truth primitive
        family alone, the system must recover the correct structure
        (NMSE $<0.05$; i.e., less than $5\%$ unexplained variance).
  \item \textbf{Ablation control.} With the ground-truth family excluded from
        an otherwise unrestricted search over the full eight-primitive
        registry, the BIC gap $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}>10$ (Kass--Raftery ``very
        strong evidence'') must hold between the domain-guided Rank-1
        candidate from the blind search and the best Rank-1 candidate found under ablation.
  \item \textbf{Determinism.} Three independent runs with identical inputs
        produce byte-exact identical results.
\end{enumerate}
Failure of any check yields WITHHELD.

classical predictions, dimensional variable definitions, and the taxonomy key are provided.

\paragraph{Screened Coulomb.}
Recovered $\theta_0(e^{-r/\theta_4}-1)$ is an exact symbolic match to the
ground truth $\theta_0(e^{-r/\lambda_D}-1)$, with $\theta_4\approx1.49$~m
recovering the Debye length $\lambda_D=1.50$~m.
Subscript $4$ (not $0$) is machine-verifiable evidence of automated discovery:
the engine assigned this subscript by enumerating four charge-dimensional
candidates before reaching the distance-ratio $r/\theta$, which was indexed
as the fifth candidate ($\theta_4$).
A manually supplied ratio would be pinned to subscript~$0$ by convention.
$\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=30.65$ far exceeds the threshold of~10;
$\Delta D=20.14$ confirms the advantage is driven by fit quality,
not search-space penalty.
Over 5 noise seeds, the verdict is 100\% stable (5/5 IDENTIFIABLE,
$\overline{\Delta\mathrm{BIC}}=76.61$, penalty-free $\overline{\Delta D + \Delta k\ln N}=71.39$).

\paragraph{Entropy Expansion.}
Because the classical baseline $S_i$ is constant, the scale-dependence test is
uninformative and mode detection falls back to an additive search. Thus, the recovered additive
correction $\theta_0\ln(1+dV/V_i)$ matches the additive ground truth
$nR\ln(1+dV/V_i)$ at class level: $\theta_0$ legitimately absorbs the additive
amplitude $nR \approx 8.314$, rather than the multiplicative ratio $nR/S_i$.
ADCD labels this \texttt{class\_only}---explicit epistemic qualification absent
from unconstrained SR outputs.
$\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=14.70>10$ supports IDENTIFIABLE; however,
$\Delta D=-1.08$ reveals the identifiability is \emph{parsimony-driven}:
the ablated search achieves an equivalent raw fit with $k{=}3$ parameters
versus $k{=}1$ for the domain-guided model.
Over 5 noise seeds, the verdict is borderline (2/5 IDENTIFIABLE,
$\overline{\Delta\mathrm{BIC}}=9.91\pm3.40$, sample SD), confirming the logarithmic
correction sits at the decision boundary under 1\% noise.

\paragraph{Time Dilation.}
At $v\le0.3c$, the Lorentz correction $\gamma-1\approx4.8\%$ of the classical
prediction---a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $4.8\!:\!1$ against the
$1\%$ noise floor, which is insufficient for reliable isolation.
The grammar recovers the Lorentz structure $D_\mathrm{lor}(v^2/c^2)$ at
Rank~1 ($\hat{\theta}_0\approx1.01$), but the positive control fails (NMSE$=0.41$): over $v\le0.3c$ (RMS correction $\approx1.6\%$ vs.\ $1\%$ noise), even the exact ground-truth curve has an intrinsic observational noise floor of $\mathrm{NMSE}\approx\sigma_\mathrm{noise}^2/\mathrm{Var}(\Delta_\mathrm{obs})\approx0.41>0.05$.
Because $>40\%$ of residual variance is measurement noise, the Positive Control gate correctly triggers WITHHELD.
Over 5 noise seeds, this verdict is 100\% stable (5/5 WITHHELD).

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Discussion}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

\textbf{WITHHELD is not failure.}
A system that always returns a structural claim regardless of data sufficiency
is epistemically weaker than one that formally distinguishes
\emph{found and confirmed} (IDENTIFIABLE) from
\emph{data insufficient for a structural claim} (WITHHELD).
ADCD's WITHHELD verdict on Time Dilation is the system correctly locating
its own identifiability boundary---a boundary that is quantitative and
testable: a wider velocity window ($v>0.3c$) or lower measurement noise ($\sigma<1\%$) would lower the observational noise floor below $0.05$, yielding IDENTIFIABLE.

\textbf{Taxonomy as prior, not hint.}
The taxonomy restricts \emph{which primitive family} is active;
the Buckingham-$\pi$ engine and optimizer determine \emph{which variable}
and \emph{which scale} within that family.
This is by design: ADCD operates as a domain-guided framework
(see Table~\ref{tab:comparison}, row ``Prior''), not a tabula-rasa search.
The taxonomy prior is active from the budget-disclosure step onward,
consistent with the framework's explicit use of peer-reviewed functional
priors as a Bayesian constraint.
The Screened Coulomb subscript $\theta_4$ is machine-verifiable evidence
that the optimizer found the correct variable independently: subscript
indices are assigned sequentially by the Buckingham-$\pi$ engine, not
by any taxonomy entry.
A $3{\times}3$ misspecification audit confirms the taxonomy is safe:
all 6 wrong-taxonomy trials yielded WITHHELD (0\% false discovery).

\textbf{Comparison with general SR.}
ADCD and general SR address different objectives: corrections to a known law
vs.\ full equation discovery from scratch.
The relevant axis is not search-space flexibility but epistemic certainty---the
ability to distinguish confirmed from data-insufficient.
Table~\ref{tab:comparison} summarises the operational regimes.

\textbf{Principle-guided discovery vs.\ black-box prediction.}
Recent perspectives on AI for physics highlight a crucial epistemic challenge:
while modern AI excels at high-dimensional predictive emulation, true physical theory
building requires compact mathematical laws, symmetry invariance, and controlled asymptotic
regimes~\cite{shalyt2026}.
ADCD explicitly embodies this principle-first paradigm: rather than performing unconstrained
curve-fitting, it converts physical correction discovery into an exact, dimensionally
consistent perturbation search anchored to established baselines and audited by falsifiable
identifiability metrics.

\begin{table}[ht]
\small
\caption{Operational comparison: ADCD vs.\ unconstrained symbolic regression.}
\label{tab:comparison}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{2.8cm}p{3.5cm}p{4.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
Property & ADCD & General SR \\
\midrule
Target & Corrections to known laws & Full equations from scratch \\
Prior & Phenomenon-specific taxonomy & None (tabula rasa) \\
Dimensional engine & 5D MLT$\Theta$Q & Varies (often 3D or none) \\
Classical limit & Algebraic guarantee & Soft loss penalty \\
Identifiability & Explicit; WITHHELD if insufficient & Absent or post-hoc \\
Reproducibility & Byte-exact deterministic & Stochastic \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

\textbf{Weak-signal convergence.}
Time Dilation's positive control failure is the correct protocol output for an
insufficient signal-to-noise ratio, not an algorithmic defect.
Future work should investigate adaptive restarts and denser initialization grids.

\textbf{Scope.}
Current support covers eight primitive families, additive and multiplicative corrections, and
synthetic Gaussian noise.
Heavier-tailed noise and real observational data
(e.g., galactic rotation curves, pulsar timing residuals) remain future work;
real data require preprocessing for heteroscedastic uncertainties not yet modelled.

\textbf{Taxonomy coverage.}
Each new entry requires a peer-reviewed derivation for every admitted family---a
deliberate constraint preventing unchecked hypothesis-space expansion.

\textbf{Safety--expressivity trade-off.}
ADCD constrains its hypothesis space relative to general-purpose SR: candidates
failing dimensional consistency or outside the phenomenon-specific primitive set
are rejected before fitting.
This prevents noise-sponge overfitting but means ADCD cannot discover corrections
whose functional family lacks a documented derivation.
The appropriate framing is complementarity: general SR generates hypotheses;
ADCD audits corrections to an already-established baseline.

\textbf{Seed stability of borderline verdicts.}
Entropy Expansion's verdict varies across noise realizations (2/5 IDENTIFIABLE,
3/5 WITHHELD), indicating the logarithmic correction sits at the identifiability
boundary under 1\% noise.
We report this transparently as a limitation of the current noise regime.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Conclusion}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

ADCD is a deterministic, correction-first framework combining algebraically
regularized primitives, a 5D (MLT$\Theta$Q) Buckingham-$\pi$ engine, and
a Phenomenon-Specific Taxonomy.
On three canonical scenarios, two yield IDENTIFIABLE results
(Screened Coulomb: $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=30.65$, exact match;
Entropy Expansion: $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=14.70$, class-level match)
and one yields a principled WITHHELD verdict (Time Dilation at $v\le0.3c$),
where the historical signal is insufficient for a confident structural claim.
Within its deliberate scope---known classical baseline, multiplicative
correction, Gaussian noise---ADCD provides stronger reproducibility and
identifiability guarantees than general-purpose SR, and furnishes an explicit
WITHHELD verdict (with associated $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}$) when those
guarantees cannot be met.

\subsection{Extended BIC Deviance and Penalty Decomposition}
\label{app:bic}

Under the Extended BIC formulation ($\mathrm{BIC} = k\ln N + N\ln\mathrm{NMSE} + 2\ln|\mathcal{C}|$), the ablation gap $\Delta\mathrm{BIC} = \mathrm{BIC}_{\mathrm{ablated}} - \mathrm{BIC}_{\mathrm{domain}}$ decomposes into pure fit quality ($\Delta D = N\ln(\mathrm{NMSE}_{\mathrm{ablated}}/\mathrm{NMSE}_{\mathrm{domain}})$), parameter parsimony ($\Delta k\ln N$), and search-space multiplicity ($2\ln(|\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{ablated}}|/|\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{domain}}|)$), as reported in Table~\ref{tab:app_bic} for $N=200$ ($\ln 200 \approx 5.30$, $\text{seed}=42$).

  \label{tab:app_bic}

\subsection{Taxonomy Cross-Misspecification Safety Audit}
\label{app:misspec}

To verify that the phenomenon-specific taxonomy prior does not induce false discoveries when misspecified, each scenario was evaluated under its true physical taxonomy key and two intentionally mismatched keys that exclude the ground-truth primitive family. As shown in Table~\ref{tab:app_misspec}, all six misspecified trials returned \textbf{WITHHELD} ($0\%$ false discovery rate): when the true primitive family is absent from the domain prior, the unrestricted ablation search outperforms the misspecified domain search ($\Delta\mathrm{BIC} \in [-1038.24, -674.62]$ on identifiable scenarios), triggering conservative abstention rather than overfitting.
